metadata.name: Compare native and llama full logits against one saved near4K oracle

oracle.arithmetic: NumPy FP32 network math; existing FP64 RoPE angle generation then FP32 sine/cosine.
oracle.kv_representation: FP16-rounded values widened to FP32 before attention and cached as FP32
oracle.norm_weights: Original BF16 checkpoint values widened to FP32 without FP16 rounding

threadpools.thread_count_evidence: Successful public pool construction with these requested counts; this llama revision has no implemented pool-count getter
threadpools.lifetime: Created once before context inference; retained across all warmups and requests

client_manifest.compiler_version:
Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin25.4.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/bin
client_manifest.source_policy: Original profiling client; linked public llama/ggml APIs, no copied kernels.

limitations: Oracle replays native consumed IDs, including supplied teacher forcing after an EOS prediction; this is not an autonomous conversation-quality test.
Native mixed-precision kernels and reduction orders differ from independent NumPy FP32 math. Calibration reports errors and never declares a tolerance pass.
A gate applies only supplied limits at selected positions; tolerances must be justified before a separate validation run, not fitted retrospectively to these measurements.
One-dimensional norm tensors stay FP32; f16 rounds only two-dimensional checkpoint matrices. No quantized-weight oracle is provided.

oracle_logits_storage.provenance: Inputs and source_hashes in this report bind checkpoint, native capture/pack evidence and oracle implementation. Each dump step consumes prompt_ids plus consumed_continuation_ids[:step].

archive_provenance.sanitization: Repository/home paths anonymized; process/host/user identifiers omitted. Embedded hashes identify original local artifacts.

scope_note: Independent NumPy comparison of frozen native12 and llama public-API v3 diagnostic captures; no timing claim. Llama logical batch2048/physical512; exact server kernel equivalence not proven. Failures do not relax the declared numerical contract.
